title: Iran condemns US attacks on commercial vessels as war crimes
summary:
Iran condemns US attacks on commercial vessels as war crimes

Iran has accused the United States of violating international law by attacking its commercial vessels and imposing a naval blockade against the country.

“The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran strongly condemns the aggressive US action of attacking Iranian commercial vessels,” the Foreign Ministry said.

Tehran described the strikes as part of Washington’s wider military campaign and “economic war” against Iran.

It said the attacks violated the UN Charter and endangered international peace, security and commercial shipping.

The ministry pledged to “firmly defend its sovereignty and national interests” against US aggression, state-sponsored terrorism, the continuing blockade and the “harassment of commercial ships”.

It added that Washington and its allies would bear responsibility for any consequences arising from continued US “aggressive and interventionist actions” in the region.

title: Iran threatens expanded strikes on US warships if blockade continues

Iran’s unified military command has warned that it could intensify and broaden attacks on US naval vessels if Washington maintains its maritime blockade and continues the “harassment of Iranian ships”.

The Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters issued the warning in a statement carried by Iran’s state broadcaster IRIB.

It came after US forces said they had struck three Iranian oil tankers earlier today.

Israeli attacks have killed five Palestinians in Gaza over the past 48 hours, while rescue workers have recovered 11 bodies from beneath the rubble, the enclave’s Health Ministry says.

Another Palestinian died from earlier wounds, bringing the number of bodies received by Gaza’s hospitals to 17. Medical facilities also treated 27 injured people.

More victims remain trapped beneath destroyed buildings or lying in the streets because ambulance and civil defence crews cannot reach them, the ministry added.

Israeli attacks have killed 1,344 Palestinians and injured 4,464 others since last October’s “ceasefire”. Rescue workers have also recovered 815 bodies from buildings destroyed by Israel during the genocide.

title: Using a VM to Contain an AI Agent
summary:
It won’t work:

My suspicion was that GPT 5.6-Cyber would succeed, but the frequency and manner of its success removed all doubt. We have to reassess sandboxing quality for capable AI agents, and in general the software stack with which they interact.

An off-the-shelf VM is not enough to contain a modern, cyber-capable AI agent. There is simply too much attack surface. Even innocuous features (like running with a display) add extra, exploitable attack surface.

title: Security Vulnerability in a Voting System
summary:
It’s a vulnerability that allows someone to recover the order of ballots cast, newly exploited with AI tools.

Nearly four years since the original vulnerability was disclosed, I was still able to use it to analyze voter behavior in Georgia (one of the 21 states that uses affected scanners) in the recent May 2026 primary.

Notably, I never touched a voting machine, exploited a network, examined source code, or accessed anything non-public.

After pointing a coding agent to the original vulnerability paper, I supplied it with two data sources highlighted in the paper: the early-voting list for each county, and the “CVR” (cast-vote record) file, containing every ballot and its selections (but not the voters’ names or other identifying information). The CVR file is available upon request, precisely because a public, ballot-level record is what makes election results independently verifiable...

title: AI Coding Agents Are Installing Unknown/Untrusted Code on Corporate Networks
summary:
We cannot forget that AI coding agents are not yet trustworthy:

Researchers at a stealth startup in Israel scanned 6,214 live domains belonging to defense contractors, Fortune 500, and Big Tech companies. Of the 8,265 llms.txt and llms-full.txt files they found (many sites hosted both an llms.txt and an llms-full.txt file), 120 of them, each on a different site, pointed to one or more code packages or domain names that weren’t registered. To test what happens when an AI agent processes such files, the researchers registered a handful of the unclaimed names and hosted packages that caused any machine executing them to reach out to their server. Within an hour, the researchers received a phone-home response from a Fortune 500 company. Over time, they got a few dozen more, some from more Fortune 500 companies and others from startups. Their beacon also recorded the chain of parent processes that spawned each install, ultimately revealing that coding agents, including Claude, OpenAI’s Codex, and Nous Research’s Hermes, were involved. Anthropic, OpenAI, and Nous Research did not respond to requests for comment by the time of publication...

title: Pentagon chief threatens more strikes on Iranian oil tankers
summary:
Pentagon chief threatens more strikes on Iranian oil tankers

US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth says the military can attack Iran’s entire oil tanker fleet, after Washington announced strikes on three Iranian vessels following attacks on US warships.

“It’s simple: if Iran shoots at US ships, we will destroy (and sink) their oil tankers. All they have to do is not shoot” at the US Navy, Hegseth posted on X.

“Iran’s oil tanker fleet is defenceless – Iran has no navy or air force,” he continued. “Our planes, ships & subs can strike them all”.

title: White House weighs replacing Pentagon number two as post-Iran war turmoil deepens
summary:
White House weighs replacing Pentagon number two as post-Iran war turmoil deepens

The White House is considering possible replacements for US Deputy Secretary of Defense Steve Feinberg as the Pentagon grapples with unusually high staff turnover, Reuters reported, citing three people familiar with the discussions.

The administration began reviewing candidates in June and consulted senior senators to assess whether its preferred nominees could secure confirmation, according to two sources. One said the process remained under way in late August.

The sources said the White House had not decided to dismiss Feinberg. They did not explain why officials were exploring alternatives or identify any of the candidates under consideration.

title: Gaza’s destroyed sewage system linked to ‘rare’ algae bloom shutting Israeli desalination plants
summary:
Gaza’s destroyed sewage system linked to ‘rare’ algae bloom shutting Israeli desalination plants

Untreated sewage from Gaza may have helped cause a huge algae bloom that shut down five of Israel’s six major desalination plants on the Mediterranean, Israeli news outlet Ynet has reported. 

Scientists are trying to assess possible environmental fallout from Gaza’s destroyed wastewater infrastructure, the report said. 

In an alarming development, the algae bloom spread along Israel's Mediterranean coast, disrupting seawater desalination plants that provide much of the country's drinking water, CNN reported, citing Mekorot, Israel's national water company.

Desalination provides at least 65 percent of Israel's drinking water, with most plants located on the coast.

“An event of this kind has never occurred before in Israel … it was an extremely rare event,” said Lior Gutman, a spokesperson for Mekorot.

title: Top US military officials face lie-detectors in leak investigation: reports
summary:
Top US military officials face lie-detectors in leak investigation: reports

The Pentagon has begun subjecting senior military officials to lie-detector tests as part of an investigation into who leaked details about US munitions stockpiles, US media reported.

Reports in July said the US was rationing some munitions, particularly missile interceptors, amid concerns over supplies following months of war with Iran.

Trump administration officials strongly rejected the claims.

President Donald Trump said the US had "a lot of ammunition, different types", while acknowledging that the military would like more of "some of the more sophisticated stuff".

The New York Times reported late on Friday that around 50 members of the military’s Joint Staff, the Pentagon’s planning and advisory body, were being required to undergo polygraph tests as part of an investigation into the leak.
